facts.raw_span: A man in his 60s with a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus
who worked as a butcher and occasional hunter and had contact with hares and rabbits
lesions on left hand evolving over 3 days
vesiculobullous lesions appeared on the dorsal aspect of his left hand and extended into the web space between the first and second fingers
the lesion extended to the palm and ventral aspect of the thumb with an eroded area on which pustules appeared
No fever or other systemic symptoms were present
Hemorrhagic bullous lesions on the dorsal aspect of left hand extending to web space between first and second fingers
Surface erosion with pustular lesions on palm and ventral aspect of thumb
Fungal culture was negative
bacterial culture showed Staphylococcus simulans
Polymerase chain reaction analysis for Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae was negative
Initially hemorrhagic bullous lesions appeared

concepts.why: The presence of Staphylococcus simulans in the bacterial culture and the description of the lesions are consistent with a staphylococcal skin infection.
The patient's occupation as a butcher and contact with hares and rabbits, along with the appearance of the lesions, could suggest erysipeloid, although the PCR test was negative.
The patient's contact with rabbits and the appearance of the lesions could suggest cutaneous tularemia, although no specific test results are provided to support this diagnosis.
The presence of pustules and the description of the lesions are consistent with pustular dermatitis, although the underlying cause is not specified.
The appearance of the lesions and the presence of Staphylococcus simulans in the bacterial culture could suggest cellulitis, although the extent of the infection is not specified.

The negative fungal culture and negative polymerase chain reaction analysis for Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae, along with the patient's contact with animals and occupation, suggest cutaneous anthrax as a possible diagnosis.

rationales.F02: Contact with hares and rabbits increases the likelihood of Erysipeloid and Cutaneous tularemia.
rationales.F10: Presence of Staphylococcus simulans in bacterial culture strongly supports Staphylococcal skin infection.
rationales.F11: Negative PCR result for Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae rules out Erysipeloid.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of Staphylococcus simulans in the bacterial culture and the characteristics of the lesions, such as vesiculobullous and hemorrhagic bullous lesions, support the diagnosis of a Staphylococcal skin infection, despite the patient's occupation and contact with animals that could suggest other zoonotic infections like Erysipeloid.
